insights.title: Six-function properties, domains and reciprocal Pythagorean choices
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie starts reciprocal definitions, exact values and Pythagorean identities, then equations and sign/existence explanations. YM revisits definitions inC4and beginsC10with reciprocal sketches and suitable-pair uniqueness arguments. Those visual arguments require both curves and a reason, not merely a calculated root.
insights.examination_comparison: 2022P2Q7(a),2023P2Q3(b)(i)and2025P2Q7(a) combine reciprocal/domain identities;2025P2Q4(b) asks a reciprocal graph. The exact official award chains remain in the marking register; the textbook method is an alternative only where valid under the original instructions.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E12/C12/A13name all six functions and reciprocal identities. Start with definitions/exact values; harder sources introduce branch domains, a shared-graph uniqueness proof or identity choice. Avoid adding formal function theory beyond the syllabus.
insights.pitfalls: cot iscos/sinand has zeros at90/270degrees; representing it as1/tan everywhere creates false holes. Goldie3C11/YMTry16Q2 keys miss90degrees after dividing bycos. Original csc/sec poles must still be excluded.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie has explicit sign-possibility discussion; YM has more reciprocal sketch scaffolding. A graph comparison is distinct from a numeric-equation drill. Visuals need coherent poles, branch extrema and angular units.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose reciprocal-definition, graph, sign and Pythagorean-equation branches. Independently evaluate every original-domain candidate; do not let the solver representation define the mathematical domain.

insights.title: Compound identities in exact evaluation, proofs and solving
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie gives a geometric sine proof and asks which assumptions it uses, then derives other formulas and applies them in exact values, equations and geometry. YM gives triangle teaching derivations, forward/reverse patterns and signed two-angle tasks. Both need conditional tangent denominators, not just the memorised numerator pattern.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q6(a)(b),2024P2Q9(b)and2025P2Q3 credit connected compound/exact reasoning. A supporting exact-value drill does not automatically cover the full show/hence chain. Native source award rows decide when a prescribed route matters.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E12/C12/A13permit compound identities for simplification, exact evaluation and solving. Harder sources change signs, require a derived ratio first, or construct the equation from geometry; exact special values alone are the entry branch.
insights.pitfalls: YM8TryQ2 swaps keys and omits one answer; its other TryQ1 printed working has a wrong sign even though the final values agree. Goldie3B3(i) has a mixed-variable stem;3B9 swaps ordered roles. Keep each as a source defect rather than an accepted learner path.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie has more assumption/coordinate-geometry work; YM gives explicit signed quadrant scaffolding. Forced complex-method facets inC11remain extra-scope original evidence even if an ordinary trig proof reaches the same result.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose exact, proof, equation, signed-given and geometry branches. Preserve requested identities/hence links and common-domain alternatives; do not label every sum-of-angles task the same problem type.

insights.title: Double-angle choices and derived higher/half forms
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie develops all three cosine-double forms, explicitly distinguishes checking from proving and motivates square reduction for calculus. YM includes repeated doubles, half-angle signs, triple proofs and connected proof/hence equations. Derived forms are legitimate consequences rather than added memorisation objectives.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q12(b),2022P2Q7(a),2023P2Q3(b)(i)and2025P2Q7(a) combine double/reciprocal identity work.2022P2Q10(b) uses sin2theta in a parametric stationary calculation: the calculus response remains connected rather than renamed a trig drill.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E12/C12/A13bound double-angle use. Harder source branches select a productive form, derive3x/4x or control a half-angle sign. General unbounded solutions remain outsideLIMIT02.
insights.pitfalls: Dividing bycosx can lose a valid original cotangent zero; introducingtan2x can create an unnecessary proof gap. The original angle interval decides the sign of a half-angle root; YM13TryQ4 prints an invalid plus branch.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie explicitly links square reduction to later integration without asking an integral there; YM gives more exact half/double ratio practice. A teaching formula derivation is not a separately examined integration task.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose identity-choice and derived-form branches with explicit domain/sign evidence. Keep proof routes that cover the full common domain and validate roots against the original expressions.

insights.title: R-form, bounded solving and transformed extrema
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie emphasises requested phase templates, arbitrary-quadrant phases and whole conversion/extrema/sketch/solve chains. YM separates degree/radian forms, multiple arguments and nonlinear range mapping. Both teach acute R triangles only under sign conditions; a general coefficient claim needs quadrant-aware phases and a nonzero pair.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q12(a),2022P2Q6and2025P2Q9 anchor conversion followed by a changed target. Their official award structure is not implied for a textbook reciprocal/square extremum variant. Keep source relatedness below a verified recipe-branch same-type claim.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E12/C12/A13name R-form use. Entry tasks compare coefficients; harder chains add phase windows, first-positive arguments, graphs or nonmonotone range maps. The current taxonomy is not a grade classification or approved branch count.
insights.pitfalls: Goldie3D6 phase67.7is wrong; YMTry19Q2 omits a root; Try20Q1 changes a sign between parts. A square minimum can be at innerzero, not the negative endpoint. Complete current cancellation has no unique phase.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie corridor geometry and current superposition offer modelling variety; YM offers many explicit nonlinear extrema. Repeated source occurrences with new tariffs do not create additional types. A diagram needs the same width/projection values as the algebra.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose prescribed-template, equation-window, graph-chain, geometry-model and nonlinear-range branches. Store the exact coefficient pair/phase, solve using original precision and test zero-amplitude/denominator cases explicitly.
